questions.domain: Retirement Accounts: IRAs, Roth IRAs, 401(k)s, and 403(b)s
questions.prompt: What is an IRA?

choices.text: An insured checking account for retirees
A government pension that is paid to every American worker
An individual retirement account with tax advantages
A loan program for people near retirement

questions.correct_answer: An individual retirement account with tax advantages
questions.intro: An IRA (individual retirement account, officially "arrangement") is a personal retirement account that you open yourself, not through an employer. IRAs give tax advantages in exchange for rules about contributions and withdrawals. Money in an IRA can be invested in stocks, bonds, funds, and more.
questions.feedback: An IRA is a personal, tax-advantaged retirement account.
sources: IRS (Publication 590-A and 590-B): IRA contributions require taxable compensation (earned income) and are limited to the lesser of the annual limit or compensation; Roth contributions are not deductible; qualified Roth distributions are tax-free. (https://www.irs.gov/retirement-plans/individual-retirement-arrangements-iras)

questions.domain: Retirement Accounts: IRAs, Roth IRAs, 401(k)s, and 403(b)s
questions.prompt: What makes an IRA a RETIREMENT account rather than an ordinary investment account?

choices.text: It can hold only cash, never investments
It is insured by the FDIC against losses
It is opened only after age 65
Tax benefits come with rules that discourage early withdrawals

questions.correct_answer: Tax benefits come with rules that discourage early withdrawals
questions.intro: IRAs get special tax treatment. In return, withdrawals of earnings before age 59½ generally face taxes and a 10% additional tax unless an exception applies.
questions.feedback: Tax advantages plus early-withdrawal rules make it a retirement account.
sources: IRS (Publication 590-A and 590-B): IRA contributions require taxable compensation (earned income) and are limited to the lesser of the annual limit or compensation; Roth contributions are not deductible; qualified Roth distributions are tax-free. (https://www.irs.gov/retirement-plans/individual-retirement-arrangements-iras)

questions.domain: Retirement Accounts: IRAs, Roth IRAs, 401(k)s, and 403(b)s
questions.prompt: Which describes a ROTH IRA?

choices.text: Contributions are made with after-tax money; qualified withdrawals are tax-free
Contributions are always tax-deductible; all withdrawals are taxed as income later
There are no taxes at any stage, including contributions
Contributions are deductible; qualified withdrawals are tax-free

questions.correct_answer: Contributions are made with after-tax money; qualified withdrawals are tax-free
questions.intro: Roth IRA: you contribute money you have already paid tax on (no deduction now). The account grows tax-free, and qualified withdrawals in retirement are tax-free.
questions.feedback: Roth = pay tax now, tax-free qualified withdrawals later.
sources: IRS (Publication 590-A and 590-B): IRA contributions require taxable compensation (earned income) and are limited to the lesser of the annual limit or compensation; Roth contributions are not deductible; qualified Roth distributions are tax-free. (https://www.irs.gov/retirement-plans/individual-retirement-arrangements-iras)

questions.domain: Retirement Accounts: IRAs, Roth IRAs, 401(k)s, and 403(b)s
questions.prompt: Which describes a TRADITIONAL IRA?

choices.text: Contributions are after-tax; qualified withdrawals are completely tax-free
Contributions may be tax-deductible; withdrawals are taxed as income
It can be opened only by employers
It pays a fixed interest rate set by law

questions.correct_answer: Contributions may be tax-deductible; withdrawals are taxed as income
questions.intro: Traditional IRA: contributions may be tax-deductible (depending on income and workplace plan coverage). The account grows tax-deferred, and withdrawals are taxed as ordinary income.
questions.feedback: Traditional = possible deduction now, taxes on withdrawals later.

misconceptions.D: Confuses an IRA with a CD or bond

sources: IRS (Publication 590-A and 590-B): IRA contributions require taxable compensation (earned income) and are limited to the lesser of the annual limit or compensation; Roth contributions are not deductible; qualified Roth distributions are tax-free. (https://www.irs.gov/retirement-plans/individual-retirement-arrangements-iras)

questions.domain: Retirement Accounts: IRAs, Roth IRAs, 401(k)s, and 403(b)s
questions.prompt: $1,000 of earnings is put toward retirement. In a Roth, tax of 12% is paid first, so $880 is invested; in a traditional IRA, the full $1,000 is invested and taxed at 12% on withdrawal. Both grow 4 times. After taxes, what does each provide?
questions.intro: Roth: tax first, then tax-free growth. Traditional: grow first, then tax. If the tax rate is the same now and later, the results match.
sources: IRS (Publication 590-A and 590-B): IRA contributions require taxable compensation (earned income) and are limited to the lesser of the annual limit or compensation; Roth contributions are not deductible; qualified Roth distributions are tax-free. (https://www.irs.gov/retirement-plans/individual-retirement-arrangements-iras)

sections.skill: Pay tax now or pay tax later
sections.relationship: The Roth versus traditional choice is a financial-concept prerequisite: when the tax is paid.

questions.prompt: With a Roth account, WHEN is income tax paid on the money you contribute?

choices.text: When it is withdrawn in retirement
Never; Roth money is never taxed

questions.intro: Two ways to get a tax break: pay tax now and skip it later (Roth), or skip tax now and pay it later (traditional).
questions.feedback: Roth contributions are made with already-taxed money.

misconceptions.B: Believes no tax is ever paid

questions.feedback: Tax diversification hedges against unknown future rates.

questions.prompt: Which account has NO required minimum distributions during the original owner's lifetime?

questions.correct_answer: A 401(k) is offered through an employer; an IRA is opened by an individual
